editorial.overview: The Certified Pediatric Nurse (CPN) exam is administered by the Pediatric Nursing Certification Board (PNCB). It measures a nurse's ability to provide care across four distinct domains: Health Promotion, Assessment, Planning and Management, and Professional Responsibilities. This certification validates clinical expertise in pediatric settings, ensuring that nurses meet the standards required to support the health and development of infants, children, and adolescents throughout their care journey. By achieving this credential, nurses demonstrate their commitment to excellence in pediatric nursing practice and patient safety.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for registered nurses who provide direct care to pediatric patients. Candidates should have clinical experience in pediatric settings and seek to demonstrate their proficiency in managing the health needs of children and their families through formal board certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official content outline provided by the Pediatric Nursing Certification Board (PNCB). Focus your study time on the four weighted domains, prioritizing the 35% allocated to Assessment and 33% to Planning and Management. Utilize official resources to understand the exam structure and question types. Practice applying clinical knowledge to pediatric scenarios to ensure you are ready for the 175 questions on the exam. Consistent review of these core areas is required for success.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers strategies for promoting health in pediatric populations. It focuses on preventative care, education, and supporting healthy development for children and their families throughout their growth and maturation processes within the clinical environment.

This domain accounts for 35% of the exam and involves the systematic collection and analysis of patient data to identify health status and potential risks in pediatric patients during various clinical encounters and nursing assessments.

This domain focuses on the development and implementation of care plans. It covers the management of interventions and the coordination of care for pediatric patients to ensure optimal health outcomes during the treatment process.

This domain addresses the professional standards and responsibilities required of a pediatric nurse, including ethical practice, legal requirements, and adherence to regulatory guidelines within the healthcare environment for all patients under their direct professional care.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared for a 180-minute testing session. Manage your time effectively across the 175 questions to ensure you address all domains. Read each question carefully to identify the specific pediatric clinical context before selecting your answer.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The CPN exam consists of 175 questions in total. These questions are distributed across four domains, with Assessment and Planning and Management making up the largest portions of the exam content for all candidates.

To achieve certification, candidates must reach a passing score of 400 scaled score. This score reflects the required level of proficiency in pediatric nursing as determined by the Pediatric Nursing Certification Board.
The exam has a total duration of 180 minutes. Candidates should plan their time carefully to complete all 175 questions within this period to ensure they have sufficient time for every section.

faq.question_title: Where can I find the current certification path?
faq.answer_text: For information regarding the current certification path or any updates to the exam requirements, please check with the Pediatric Nursing Certification Board (PNCB) directly for the most accurate and official guidance.
